simple.meaning: גָּעָה (gâʻâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to bellow (as cattle).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in 1 Samuel, Job, beginning at 1 Samuel 6:12. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּעָה (H1600) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּעָה (gâʻâh) / H1600 is traced through 1 Samuel 6:12, Job 6:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1600. gaah גָּעָה verb low (of cattle) (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic גְּעָא , ) — יִגְעֶהשֿׁוֺר Job 6:5 ; וְגָעוֺ הָלֹךְ 1Sam 6:12 .

occurrences.englishText: The cows took the straight way by the way to Beth Shemesh. They went along the highway, lowing as they went, and didn’t turn away to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines went after them to the border of Beth Shemesh.
Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass?
